notes: GRADER-ASSERTION BUG, not a skill gap: the limiter assertion forbade any time.Sleep, but sleeping INSIDE a synctest bubble is the idiomatic way to advance virtual time. All three with_skill runs used synctest correctly with bubble-internal sleeps; corrected, limiter with_skill is effectively 6/6 on all three models vs 4/6 baseline (real sleeps, in-package test).

JUDGMENT CALL the doctrine itself forces: every with_skill run DELETED config's sleep-based concurrent-use smoke rather than rewriting it — defensible because the package documents no concurrency contract, so the test pinned a promise never made. The assertion assumed a rewrite. Maintainer input wanted: should config promise concurrent reads (then a synctest test pins it) or is deletion correct?

REAL CROSS-MODEL GAP: sonnet with_skill collapsed on config-test-review (3/8, below the 5/8 baseline) — it deleted the scaffold and fixed the internals-reach but kept per-symbol grain, self-naming doc comments, the empty benchmark, and added no Examples. The review-shaped task ('dont break anything') seems to suppress restructuring on sonnet; fable/opus with_skill hit 7/8. Candidate iteration-2 fix: an explicit 'reviewing an existing suite' clause.

UNIVERSAL MISS, skill or no skill: units-add-test — every run added a standalone per-function-named TestParseDurationOrDefault instead of a behavior-named scenario or an Example (fable/opus at least made it table-driven). The 'add a test for X' prompt gravity beats the naming doctrine on all models; the skill needs an explicit clause. Assertion may also soften: a NEW behavior-named table is legitimate when the existing table doesn't fit.
Tokens are not observable per-run inside a workflow; token columns are zeroed. time_seconds are agent-self-reported wall-clock.
